content: Does anyone know of any formalization work on the natural well-ordering problem in proof theory? I feel like it would be extremely amenable to progress in Lean for both technical and methodological reasons, but I can't seem to find anyone within even a mile radius of it.

For example, in our project FFL, we have some experimental formalizations for proof theory by Claude: the unprovability of Goodstein's theorem in PA, cut elimination, consistency of PA, and so on.
In light of this experiment, we think it would be better to redesign and rework the whole thing, so the repository itself is somewhat abandoned at the moment.

https://github.com/FormalizedFormalLogic/goodstein-independence/blob/4eb213ca8220115afdb2b6ae28b9e1e535bd1577/GoodsteinPA/Result/ConsistencyPA.lean

I have not heard of anyone else doing proof theory in Lean.
Interesting, would you consider the experiment a success?

This experiment itself is a refactoring of Trevor Morris @Trevor Morris 's project, which we took over under FFL.
I've confirmed that the facts given as examples can be formalized sorry-free, but the code itself is chaotic and I think it needs to be reimplemented. Also, since I don't have much expertise in proof theory, it's difficult to expect further development here (at least from me).
That said, I consider the experiment itself a success.

I would make a comment to the effect of "trust me, proof theory isn't that bad, its actually quite fun!" But that's tough for me to say with a straight face given that I also have decided it is both good and wise to eschew propext, classical.choice, and Quot.sound completely. Still, it warms my heart to see others take interest.
